text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"NJ","level":"state","category":"security_deposits","status":"in_force","title":"New Jersey Security Deposit Law: deposit cap, prepaid rent, annual increases, interest-bearing account","requirement":"A landlord is not required to collect a security deposit, but if one is collected the landlord must follow the Security Deposit Law. The deposit may not exceed one and one-half times one month's rent. Any yearly increase in the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. A pet security deposit may not push the combined total above 1.5 times monthly rent. Prepaid funds held to secure future rent, including last month's rent, count as part of the security deposit. At lease inception the landlord may require only the deposit (max 1.5x monthly rent) plus the first month's rent, so no more than 2.5x monthly rent in total. Deposit money stays the tenant's property and is held in trust, not commingled with the landlord's funds. A landlord or designee holding deposits for ten or fewer units must keep them in an insured New Jersey bank or savings and loan in an interest-bearing account. A landlord holding deposits for 10 or more units may instead use an insured New Jersey money market fund (investments maturing in one year or less) or a New Jersey bank or savings and loan account bearing a variable rate. Interest or earnings belong to the tenant. When a tenant ends a lease under the Safe Housing Act (domestic violence), the landlord must make the deposit plus interest available within 15 business days. The landlord must also give written notice of pick-up time and place within 3 business days, with an itemized list of interest and deductions.","key_value":"Max deposit 1.5x one month's rent; yearly increase max 10% of current deposit; max 2.5x monthly rent at lease inception (deposit plus first month); interest belongs to tenant","coverage_conditions":"Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
